notes:
The whole list is on n22.jpg (printed p. 11). n21.jpg (p. 10) has only the lead-in and the key to the class numerals. n23.jpg (p. 12) begins 'Diary from the Stations'.

Layout: the list is headed 'EAST OF SCOTLAND.' with the subheads Shetland. / Orkney. / Mainland. in small caps. The columns are: 'Returns in 5 years.' (a count); '1884.' (an asterisk for a return this year); map number; station, with a county or island for the Shetland and Mainland rows only (the Orkney rows have none); class numeral I.–V., sometimes with '(a)'; 'Feet.' (height); keeper. There are no L.H./L.V. abbreviations and no light-character descriptions. The class numeral is the committee's 'migration value', not the light's character, so I put it in other and left character null. Footnote (a) on the page reads: 'Notwithstanding the favourable description of light.' Below the list: 'NOTE.—Read in this place part of the General Remarks at the end of West Coast of Scotland.'

Transcription conventions: in the printed field I wrote the leader dots as runs of dots; their exact count isn't reliable. In the name, place and keepers fields I dropped the full stop or dots that end a row (e.g. 'T. Edgar.' → 'T. Edgar'). Abbreviation stops ('N.', 'St.', 'Jos.') are kept. In the Mainland rows the place follows a comma after the name.

Numbering: the list runs from 4 to 29, i.e. 26 stations. Numbers 1–3 are not here, presumably Faroe and Iceland, which the lead-in says the 'thirty stations' include. Twelve rows have the 1884 asterisk (4, 7, 8, 14, 15, 19, 20, 22, 24, 26, 27, 28). That matches the text's 'Twelve stations on East Coast of Scotland have sent in forty-one schedules'.

Oddity: Kinnaird Head (22) has an 1884 asterisk but nothing in the 'Returns in 5 years' column. This suggests the 5-year count covers 1879–83 and leaves out 1884. In this old-style type '3' looks like '8' and '5' looks like '6'. I read them as 3 and 5, since no count can be above 5; the OCR agrees.

Stray marks: a speck after the '3' in the Whalsey Skerries returns column, and a dot before 'V.' in the Kinnaird Head row. Neither looks like a real mark.

Spellings and places to keep as printed, not correct: 'Whalsey' (Whalsay); 'N. Ronaldshay'; 'Girdleness' and 'Montroseness' each printed as one word; 'Inch Keith' as two words; 'East Cromarty'; 'Holborn Head'. Chanonry Point is given as 'Elgin' though it is on the Ross-shire (Black Isle) side of the firth. Dunnet Head (Caithness) is printed under the Orkney subhead.

Keepers: only 8 are named in the list. The Sumburgh keeper's surname may be printed 'Soott' (broken c); the OCR and the footnote give 'Scott' (see that row's unsure). The OCR's split-off lines 1482–1483 ('.(a) 175 B.S. Ritson.', '60 John McGill.') belong to Tarbat Ness (18) and Cromarty (19), and the image reads 'R. S. Ritson', not 'B.S.'.

People named in the diary on p. 12 (n23) but not in the list, useful for the roll:
- N. Unst: 'Mr. James Edgar—formerly at Butt of Lewis', the list's 'T. Edgar'. The initials disagree, so the 'T.' may be a misprint.
- N. Ronaldshay: 'Mr. John Tulloch', who sent one schedule.
- Pentland Skerries: 'Mr. J. Gilmour'.
- Sumburgh Head, in a footnote: 'Mr. D. M.. Scott has removed to Lamlash, Arran, since the date of his last schedule, Sept. 15th, 1884, and is succeeded by Mr. Youngclause from Monach Islands.'
